text:
[on screen: A list of what the next ten years should bring, written on a quiet evening.] A list of what the next ten years should bring, written on a quiet evening.
[on screen: Katha Upaniṣad 1.2.1-2] There is an old text that says it plainly. The good and the pleasant differ, the Kaṭha says; both come to a person, and the wise tell them apart.
Here is what the passage says, closely: Yama tells Naciketas: the good (śreyas) is one thing, the pleasant (preyas) another; both bind a person. Both come to a person; the wise one examines and distinguishes them, and prefers the good. The fool chooses the pleasant for getting and keeping.
The Kaṭha does not sort anyone's list; it says each of the two binds a person to its own aim.
Where the text stops: it names the two and the wise one's preference; it does not say which item on a list is which.
[on screen: What is each item on the list for?] What is each item on the list for?

cite.title: Katha Upaniṣad
cite.original: śreyaś ca preyaś ca manuṣyam etas tau samparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ | śreyo hi dhīro 'bhi preyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yogakṣemād vṛṇīte
cite.paraphrase: The good (śreyas) is one thing, the pleasant (preyas) another; both bind a person with different aims. Good comes to one who takes the good; one who chooses the pleasant misses the goal. Both come to a person; the wise one examines and distinguishes them; the wise prefers the good to the pleasant; the fool chooses the pleasant for the sake of getting and keeping (yogakṣema).
